Polish Security Services Probe Plot Targeting Tusk — Polish security services convened an emergency meeting on Sunday, Oct. 11, following reports of a possible assassination plot targeting Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, the Interior Ministry said. Officials from the police, State Protection Service, and Internal Security Agency gathered at Warsaw’s Counterterrorism Center as ministers ordered immediate protective measures.

Woman Killed, 10 Injured in Kharkiv Guided Bomb Strike — A Russian guided aerial bomb strike hit the Nemyshlianskyi district of Kharkiv on Sunday, Oct. 11, killing a 35-year-old woman and injuring ten civilians, including a 7-year-old boy. The bombardment destroyed two private homes, damaged 15 others, and set several vehicles ablaze near an auto repair facility, while emergency crews suppressed fires and treated the wounded.

Russian Strikes Injure 9 in Sloviansk, Sumy Region — Russian strikes on Sunday, Oct. 11, injured nine people across the Donetsk and Sumy regions. An airstrike struck two multi-story apartment buildings in Sloviansk, wounding four residents, while an early morning drone strike hit an emergency medical crew in Sumy region’s Yampil community, injuring a driver and a paramedic. The incidents follow weekend strikes that also damaged a residential high-rise in Dnipro.

Can Trump Sidestep Russia Sanctions as the Midterms Loom? — The Graham sanctions law reaches its first major implementation deadline just over two weeks before the US midterms. With Republicans at risk of losing Congress, Trump faces competing pressures from sanctions supporters, Democratic critics, and concerns about the economic consequences of new tariffs.

Kyiv Urges Residents to Stockpile Food and Water Amid Grid Hits — The Kyiv City State Administration advised capital residents on Sunday, Oct. 11, to stockpile at least three days of food and water, charge portable batteries, and insulate living spaces ahead of winter following Russian attacks on regional energy facilities. Interview: Georgian Conductor Nikoloz Rachveli on Music, Ukraine and Solidarity — Georgian conductor Nikoloz Rachveli has supported Ukraine since the first days of Russia’s full-scale invasion. In spring 2022, he performed in the Kyiv metro, helped raise funds for Ukraine and has since returned repeatedly. In an interview with Kyiv Post, Rachveli discusses music as a weapon, composer Giya Kancheli, Ukrainian composers and his hopes for a peaceful future for both Ukraine and his native Georgia.

Ukraine Ready to Halt Refinery Strikes for Energy Truce, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries if Moscow stops targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure, stressing that any de-escalation requires reciprocal commitments and verifiable guarantees. Zelensky noted Russia launched roughly 1,450 glide bombs, 75 missiles, and over 1,640 drones over the week, while search operations in Zaporizhzhia ended with 23 dead.

US Proposes Economic Incentives to Russia for Limited Truce — The Trump administration has proposed three economic incentives to Moscow – unlocking up to $100 billion in frozen assets, approving a Lukoil portfolio buyout, and easing sanctions on Belarusian potash – to secure a limited energy or maritime ceasefire with Ukraine. Zaporizhzhia Bombing Death Toll Reaches 20 as Rescue Ends — Search and rescue operations in Zaporizhzhia concluded on Sunday, Oct. 11, following a Russian guided aerial bomb strike that killed 20 people, including four children, and injured 17 others. Emergency workers cleared 320 metric tons of debris, with canine units from Donetsk and Dnipropetrovsk regions aiding the operation as municipal authorities declared a day of mourning and transitioned to site recovery.

Trump: Putin Wants Ukraine Deal, Praises Russian Oil Supplies — US President Donald Trump stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin strongly desires a settlement to conclude the war in Ukraine, claiming that President Volodymyr Zelensky has refused to make a deal. Trump also commended Putin for supplying large quantities of oil at low prices, following the announcement of a bilateral diesel agreement and renewed calls for leadership change in Kyiv.

Elon Musk Echoes Trump in Calling for New Ukrainian Leadership — American billionaire Elon Musk backed US President Donald Trump’s calls for Ukraine to replace President Volodymyr Zelensky, saying that the Ukrainian leader had “gone too far.” Musk’s comments came after Trump claimed Zelensky missed chances to end the war and criticized Ukrainian refinery strikes following a controversial bilateral diesel deal with Vladimir Putin. Only Ukrainians Decide Leadership, Sybiha Says — Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha responded to US President Donald Trump’s statements suggesting Ukraine replace President Volodymyr Zelensky, declaring that only the Ukrainian public has the right to decide its leadership. Sybiha stated that external criticism confirms Zelensky is performing his duties effectively, coming after Trump criticized refinery strikes and defended a commercial diesel pact with Moscow.

Airport Strike Kills 12, Saudi Coalition Vows ‘Decisive’ Response — A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and wounded 309 others on Saturday, Oct. 10, marking the deadliest attack on Saudi territory in more than a decade. The Saudi-led military coalition blamed Yemen’s Houthi movement for the attack, calling it a war crime and vowing a decisive response, while US President Donald Trump signaled Washington may join military actions.

US Lawmakers Draft Bill to Block Russian Oil Purchases — US Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick and Don Bacon are preparing the bipartisan “Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act” to prohibit purchases of Russian petroleum, directly challenging Donald Trump’s commercial agreement permitting Russian diesel imports. Drones Hit Yandex Data Center in Vladimir, Russia, Disrupting Over 80 Services — A Ukrainian drone strike disabled a major Yandex data center in Vladimir, Russia, early Sunday morning, Oct. 11, shutting down the 50-megawatt facility and disrupting more than 80 digital platforms, AI tools, and Yandex Cloud services across Russia and abroad. The strike marks the third attack on Yandex server hubs in four days following previous hits in Ryazan and Kaluga regions.

There Will be no Breakthrough in Peace Talks, - Stefan Korshak — Kyiv Post Senior Defense Correspondent Stefan Korshak joins TVP World to discuss recent Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and how accelerating deployments of jet-powered strike drones are straining air defenses and electricity transmission capacity ahead of winter as bilateral talks with Washington proceed under low expectations for peace negotiations.

Ukraine Should Keep Striking Russian Refineries, Kellogg Says — Retired General Keith Kellogg, former US special envoy for Ukraine, stated that Ukraine should continue drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, warning that Vladimir Putin’s diesel deal is an attempt to escape industrial pressure. US Envoys Witkoff, Kushner May Visit Russia Soon — US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Russia within the next two weeks, Russian state agency TASS reported. The prospective trip follows a telephone call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in which the Russian leader spurned peace talks and vowed to press ahead with the war, as well as inconclusive multilateral consultations in Miami and controversy over a US-Russian diesel agreement.

Russian Strike Hits Dnipro High-Rise, 4 Injured, Including 2 Children — A Russian strike damaged the eighth and ninth floors of a residential high-rise in Dnipro late Saturday, Oct. 10, injuring four people, including two eight-year-old girls, Mayor Borys Filatov reported. Rescuers detected a gas leak and severed utilities to secure the building as emergency teams assisted residents, following an earlier fatal drone strike in the region’s Nikopol district that killed an 11-year-old boy.

Its adoption showcases Moscow’s ability to secure diplomatic support against economic pressure while retaining a Security Council veto over action concerning its own conduct.

Child Killed, 2 Injured in Drone Strike Near Nikopol — An 11-year-old boy was killed and two other children – a 12-year-old boy and a 10-year-old girl – were wounded when Russian forces dropped a munition from a drone in Dnipropetrovsk region’s Pokrovska community. Slovak opposition party SaS condemned Prime Minister Robert Fico’s government on Friday, Oct. 9, calling the boycott an international disgrace and de facto collaboration with the Kremlin.

Putin’s Vile Chess — Vladimir Putin’s invasion has become a military, economic and diplomatic trap. Ukraine’s resilience, strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and growing Western backing continue to expose Moscow’s weakening position, while attacks on civilians deepen international outrage. Tougher sanctions, more weapons, the release of frozen Russian assets and lasting security guarantees are urgently needed.

Speaking alongside German AfD politicians, he said he hoped to one day proclaim his love for “the smell of Russian gas in the morning.” His remarks drew condemnation from Poland’s energy minister as US and Russian officials explored a possible pipeline deal.

Dutch Minister Calls Russia ‘The Enemy’; Russia Demands Clarification — Dutch Minister of Defence Dilan Yeşilgöz called Russia “the enemy” during a parliamentary budget debate, citing escalating threats across Europe. Russia’s embassy demanded clarification on whether the remark reflected official policy or signaled confrontation, while Yeşilgöz stressed that the Netherlands was not at war.

Belarus Summons Ukraine Envoy Over Alleged Bryansk Drone Strike — Belarus summoned Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires on Friday, Oct. 9, accusing Ukrainian forces of deliberately striking a Belarusian commercial truck in Russia’s Bryansk region that injured a citizen. Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi rejected the claim as groundless and provocative, protesting the summons and condemning Minsk for attempting to fabricate security threats while actively aiding Moscow’s war effort.

Allies Press Greece, Spain for Expiring Patriot Missiles — NATO and EU officials are pressing Greece and Spain to transfer Patriot PAC-2 interceptors nearing their 23-year shelf-life limit to Ukraine. With Kyiv requiring up to 360 interceptors for winter defense, and US stockpiles dipping below 1,700 due to operations in the Middle East, European allies are seeking to unlock southern European arsenals.

Latvia’s Pro-Ukraine Landslide Hides a Weakness Putin Could Exploit — Latvia’s election gave PM Kulbergs a strong mandate, but just 51.8% of eligible voters participated. For a NATO frontline state bordering Russia and Belarus, the weak turnout highlights concerns about social cohesion and the resilience of its internal defenses.

US Envoys Pressure Kyiv on Refinery Strikes — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have warned Ukrainian negotiators in Miami that Washington could restrict intelligence sharing if Kyiv continues striking Russian oil refineries. A US official confirmed the envoys urged Kyiv not to hurt US consumers, adding that Donald Trump struck a Russian diesel deal with Vladimir Putin after President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected a unilateral strike pause without a mutual energy ceasefire.

Finland Approves 35th Military Aid Package for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb approved the delivery of Finland’s 35th military aid package to Ukraine on Friday, Oct. 9, following an urgent appeal from Kyiv. Valued at approximately €1 million ($1.1 million), the shipment draws a single defense product from military stockpiles, bringing total Finnish defense assistance to €3.6 billion ($4 billion) as preparations begin for a broader upcoming package.

The terminal, which handles roughly 2.5 million metric tons of petroleum products annually from the Novoshakhtinsk refinery to supply the Russian military and export markets, was struck as regional authorities claimed over 50 drones were intercepted.

While Moscow uses regional trade networks to reduce Western financial pressure, the bloc faces declining political influence. Azerbaijan will chair the CIS in 2028, while Lukashenko hopes Armenia will follow in 2029.

US Republicans Join Democrats in Warning Trump’s Russia Diesel Deal Will Hurt, Not Help — Republican Representatives Don Bacon and Michael McCaul joined Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal in criticizing Trump’s Russian diesel agreement. Former US Ambassador Steven Pifer told Kyiv Post the deal would undermine peace efforts without significantly lowering fuel prices.

Two-Day Miami Peace Talks Wrap Up First Day, Overshadowed by Trump’s Putin Diesel Deal — US, Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami on Friday for peace talks initially planned to last two days. The discussions were overshadowed by Trump’s surprise diesel agreement with Putin. No breakthrough was announced, and Witkoff did not confirm whether talks would resume Saturday.

Russian Guided Bombs Strike 5-Story Residential Building in Zaporizhzhia – People Feared Trapped — Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia with guided aerial bombs early Saturday, Oct. 10, hitting a five-story residential building. Regional officials warned that people could be trapped beneath the rubble as emergency crews responded.

Trump Names Truth Social Adviser Katie Zacharia as New White House Press Secretary — US President Donald Trump has selected Katie Zacharia, a senior communications adviser at Truth Social, as the new White House press secretary. Zacharia previously served as a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson and worked on Trump’s presidential campaigns.

Ex-US Ambassador: Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal Won’t Lower Prices but Will Undermine Peace — In an exclusive Kyiv Post interview, former US Ambassador to Ukraine Steven Pifer called Donald Trump’s decision to ease Russian diesel sanctions “very unwise,” warning it would help finance Moscow’s war, undermine peace negotiations and have little impact on US fuel prices.

Kyiv Urges Graham Sanctions as Trump Cuts Deal With Putin — Zelensky urged a bipartisan US congressional delegation visiting Kyiv to enforce the Lindsey Graham sanctions law and accelerate joint Patriot interceptor production. The meeting took place under a Russian drone threat, as Trump struck a diesel deal with Putin that could provide Moscow with fresh revenue to sustain its invasion.

Zelensky: Ukrainian Peace Team in Florida Used as ‘Smokescreen’ for US-Russia Diesel Deal — President Zelensky delivered a blistering rebuke of Washington for easing sanctions on Russian diesel while Ukrainian officials negotiated peace in Florida, warning that Donald Trump was handing Vladimir Putin fresh resources to prolong the war.

Russian Drones Threaten Kyiv and Multiple Ukrainian Regions in Early Hours of Saturday — Russian forces continued launching drones across Ukraine in the early hours of Saturday, Oct. 10, triggering air raid alerts in Kyiv and other regions.

Trump Says He and Putin Have Cut Diesel Deal, Zelensky Accuses Washington of ‘Weakness’ — US President Donald Trump announced that Russia would supply diesel to global markets. Shortly after, the US Treasury Department authorized the sale and import of Russian diesel fuel through April 7, 2027. President Volodymyr Zelensky called it an “obvious weakness.”

Ukraine's Inflation Jumps to 10% as Prices Post Sharpest Monthly Spike This Year — Ukraine's annual inflation accelerated to 10.0% in September from 8.1% in August, as consumer prices rose 2.1% month-on-month, the State Statistics Service reported. Core inflation climbed to 8.8% from 8.1%, breaking a three-month plateau, while food, education and transport costs all accelerated sharply.

Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Nearly 40 Times, Killing 1 and Setting Warehouses Ablaze — Russia struck the Dnipropetrovsk region with drones, artillery and missiles nearly 40 times on Friday, Oct. 9, killing one person. According to the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, Russia struck a logistics company’s warehouses in Dnipro district twice during the evening, causing fires.

Ukrainian Drone Tech Firms Launch Thermal Sensor Project in Europe and US — The Fourth Law and Odd Systems have unveiled Project Foundation, an initiative to mass-produce uncooled thermal sensors in Europe and the US from 2027. The companies say the project aims to quadruple European output and double US output within three years. Headquartered in Eindhoven, it plans to use partner production lines and dedicated facilities, although financing details have not been disclosed.

Sybiha Presses WTO Chief on Black Sea Shipping, Remote Audits — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke with World Trade Organization (WTO) chief Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala to back efforts on restoring Black Sea shipping safety, as Russian attacks on civilian vessels and ports threaten Ukraine’s grain exports and global food security. Sybiha also sought support for a WTO standard on remote audits.

US Congress Delegation Backs Expanded Starlink Access for Ukraine — A US congressional delegation visiting Kyiv on Friday, Oct. 9 backed efforts to persuade Elon Musk to expand Ukraine’s Starlink access, Ukrinform reported. The remarks came as Kyiv seeks to use the satellite network for drone strikes on Russian missile launchers – a request US President Donald Trump reportedly declined to support.

The move, announced only hours after a former ICC judge won the Nobel Peace Prize, escalates a previous US campaign against the court over its Israel and Afghanistan probes.
